title: Ada Lovelace and the Analytical Engine
text: Ada Lovelace wrote notes on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine. Her notes described how a machine might manipulate symbols and included a method for calculating Bernoulli numbers.

title: Charles Babbage's Mechanical Computing Designs
text: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine. The Analytical Engine used a store and a mill, concepts often compared with memory and a processor in later computing explanations.

title: History of Mathematical Tables
text: Mathematical tables supported navigation, astronomy, and engineering before electronic computers. Repeated calculations motivated efforts to mechanize arithmetic and reduce transcription errors.

title: Early Programming Concepts
text: Early descriptions of programmable machines explored sequences of operations, stored values, and symbolic instructions. These ideas later became central to computer programming and software design.

title: Astronomy and Observation in the Nineteenth Century
text: Astronomers used observations and mathematical calculations to create tables, compare predictions with measurements, and document uncertainty in scientific results.
